newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian shares edge up in moderate trade.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian shares edge up in moderate trade.

text.p: Lithuanian shares edged up on Friday, regaining some of the ground they lost last week when the market fell sharply after a brief bull run.
The group A index rose by 38.52 points to 2,717.75 and central market volume was almost 2.6 million litas.
Lithuania Gas was the most active blue chip stock, rising to 2.37 litas from 2.35 litas in trade of almost 390,000 litas.

Commercial banks attracted little interest despite a recent Nomura report which said the sector was a good place to invest now. Dealers say investors are waiting for the 1996 final results from the sector.
The volume on the secondary T-bill market was over 12 million litas for the second straight day but dealers said that it was not part of a long-term trend.
"It seems that one bank sold some of its paper because it needed cash. The yields are still low and so there is not very much interest in the secondary T-bill market right now," one dealer said.
There were also over 1.8 million litas of bloc trades made on Friday.
